text:
matt_w: Flagging a reproducible oddity in spec-decoding + ql4 bringup. Short summary: a small fraction (~0.2%) of responses are missing the final token when speculative candidate is used.
lina: missing final token as in truncated sentence or abrupt stop token?
matt_w: abrupt stop, like the model emits nothing for the last token. Happens only when spec path merges early and for inputs with heavy punctuation at the end.
omar: any error logs? merge mismatch?
benchbot: quick run: model=ember-7b-ql4, speculative=true, runs=5000, truncations=11 (0.22%), median_lat=84ms, p95=330ms
benchbot: sample truncated output (input ends with "...summary:"): "The final answer is that the system will" [EOF]
gina: could be off-by-one at the candidate-vs-main path boundary. speculative candidate length calculation maybe drops last token if last token is punctuation and candidate shorter.
talia: can we reproduce deterministically? provide seed and input.
matt_w: reproduced with seed=101 and input=long-bullet-8. Repro path attached in artifacts.
ci-bot: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-test-artifacts/spec-trunc/6172839456/{cases,logs}.zip
lina: quick hypothesis: tokenizer normalizes punctuation differently on the cheap tokenizer used by spec actor. If spec actor removes a trailing punctuation token, merge thinks candidate ended earlier.
omar: another angle: our detokenizer might drop a final token if it is 0x00 or control char after merging; check buffer fill code.
gina: I ran a diff on token ids pre/post merge for a failing case: candidate path token_ids length=47, main path expects 48. The candidate had merged two punctuation tokens into one during cheap tokenization.
matt_w: so tokenization divergence between paths confirmed. That explains off-by-one truncation.
talia: mitigation options: (1) align tokenization pipeline between spec and main, (2) have merge logic use raw byte lengths instead of token counts, (3) conservative fix: when merge size mismatch, expand candidate by re-running final step with main tokenizer.
lina: (1) is ideal but might cost perf. (3) is targeted and could be a good short-term patch.
omar: agree. implement fallback: on merge_size_mismatch, re-run final candidate generation with verified tokenizer and append missing token(s). Need to be careful about latency and double-run costs.
gina: we should also add telemetry: count merge_size_mismatch, sample pre/post token_ids, and record whether fallback corrected output.
benchbot: after applying fallback for failing seeds only (recompute final tokens), test run: runs=5200, truncations=0, median_lat=88ms, p95=335ms, extra_recomputes=11 (0.21%)
matt_w: perf cost very small since recomputes only for failing merges. This seems like a practical canary patch.
talia: long-term, schedule tokenization unification. Opening a tracking ticket for tokenizer alignment across spec and main pathways.
lina: also add unit tests that fuzz punctuation-heavy endings and assert merge invariants.
omar: PR checklist: runtime fallback + telemetry, unit tests, and a small note in the onboarding doc to include punctuation-heavy long inputs in smoke matrix.
ci-bot: created PR #4127 (spec-runtime: fallback on merge mismatch) and issue #998 (spec/main tokenizer alignment).
gina: good. I'll run a 50k sample overnight with fallback enabled to ensure no other regressions crop up.
benchbot: overnight run queued. I'll post results tomorrow AM.
matt_w: thanks team. If overnight looks clean, we can promote to canary with fallback for now and continue tokenizer work in parallel.
lina: sounds good. :thumbsup:
